title: Clarinet Quintet in B minor
hook: Brahms meant to stop composing, then heard a clarinettist and wrote this autumnal farewell.

painting.title: Interior with Young Woman Seen from the Back
painting.pairingNote: A woman turned away in a grey, silent room, painted a decade after the quintet; the same hushed, inward mood as Brahms’s late chamber music.

facts: In 1890 Brahms, aged 57, thought he had written enough and could retire. In March 1891 he heard Richard Mühlfeld, the clarinettist of the court orchestra at Meiningen, and that summer at Bad Ischl in the Austrian Alps he wrote two works for him: a Clarinet Trio and this Quintet.
Mühlfeld first played it in private at Meiningen on 24 November 1891, with the Joachim Quartet. The public premiere followed in Berlin on 12 December.
The line-up is Mozart’s: one clarinet and a string quartet. Mühlfeld had played Mozart’s Clarinet Quintet for Brahms, and Brahms ends his own with a set of [[variation|variation]]s, as Mozart did.
The quintet ends where it began: the last pages of the finale bring back the opening of the first movement.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a restless, autumnal Allegro (I), a slow song with a wild, gypsy-style middle (II), a gentle tune that turns into a quick dance (III), variations that lead back to the start (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] that seems unsure of its key: the opening hovers between B minor and D major, and it takes several bars after the clarinet’s entry for B minor to settle. The mood swings between tenderness and outbursts, and the end is quiet.

mainIdeas.name: The opening
mainIdeas.description: two violins in a wavering, rocking figure, a few soft bars that will return at the very end of the work.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: the clarinet’s soft, rising arpeggio, followed by a broad, swinging tune in viola and cello.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a warmer tune in D major, sung by the clarinet over an off-beat murmur in the strings.

The clarinet slides in with a soft, rising arpeggio

stops.hear: Cello and viola, strong, play a broad, swinging tune

stops.hear: The cello, then the viola, murmur off the beat; the clarinet sings a warmer tune
Loud accents on weak beats over trembling strings
The clarinet’s arpeggio again

stops.hear: The clarinet’s arpeggio once more, but the strings turn to a darker key
Slower and hushed; long chords

notice: Listen for the opening violin figure at ≈ 0:00, then at ≈ 11:30. Brahms leaves it out of the repeat, only hints at it in the recapitulation, and saves it whole for the end.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Leister played in the Berlin Philharmonic for thirty years from 1959. The Amadeus Quartet kept its four founding members from 1947 until it disbanded in 1987.

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.summary: A slow movement in three parts. The outer parts are a quiet song for clarinet over [[muted|muted]] strings. The middle part bursts into a free, florid lament in the Hungarian “gypsy” style Brahms loved.

mainIdeas.name: The main melody
mainIdeas.description: a slow, rocking song for the clarinet, answered and shadowed by the first violin.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: wailing clarinet runs over trembling strings, like an improvisation.

stops.hear: The clarinet sings a slow, rocking melody over hazy, muted strings
stops.happening: The main theme. The strings keep their mutes on for the whole movement

stops.hear: The first violin takes the melody; the clarinet shadows it, a little behind the beat
stops.happening: The two lead voices change places

stops.hear: Clarinet and first violin play the melody together, an octave apart
stops.happening: The first part draws to a close

stops.hear: The music turns to B minor; the clarinet steals in, very quietly
The clarinet breaks into free, wailing runs over trembling strings
stops.happening: The “gypsy” style, with [[tremolo|tremolo]] in the strings

stops.hear: The clarinet, very loud and high, cries out
stops.happening: The climax: the only *fortissimo* in the movement

stops.hear: Fast trembling in the strings; the clarinet’s last runs sink to its lowest notes
The opening melody returns, as quiet as before
A last echo of the middle section’s runs, then a soft close

notice: Compare the clarinet’s sound at ≈ 0:00 and ≈ 3:26: the same instrument, first breathing a song, then almost singing out of control.

movements.heading: Andantino – Presto non assai, ma con sentimento
movements.tempo: Andantino – Presto non assai, ma con sentimento
movements.summary: A short movement in two speeds. A gentle, simple tune in D major turns into a quick, light dance in B minor, which then slips back into the gentle tune.

stops.hear: The clarinet plays a simple, gentle tune; the strings no longer have mutes
The violins add a little zigzag figure
stops.happening: A new idea that drives the next section

stops.hear: Faster: the first violin flits through a light, skittering version of the tune
stops.happening: The Presto, in B minor. The same notes, in a new rhythm

stops.hear: The clarinet leads an off-beat melody over plucked strings
The quick music seems to slow down and melts into the opening

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The last bars of the gentle tune
stops.happening: A quiet close in D major

movements.heading: Con moto
movements.summary: A theme and five [[variation|variation]]s in B minor. Each variation keeps the theme’s shape but changes its character. In the last minutes the opening of the first movement returns, and the work ends in quiet resignation.

stops.hear: The strings play a calm, songlike theme in two halves; the clarinet joins
The cello leads, alone at first, in wide arching lines
Agitated: surging, off-beat repeated notes; violin and clarinet in fragments
The clarinet plays wide, detached runs over halting chords
B major; clarinet and first violin pass gentle phrases back and forth
stops.happening: Variation 4. The only variation in the major

stops.hear: The viola leads a lilting, melancholy waltz
The first violin slides into the rocking figure that opened the first movement

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The clarinet leads the closing phrases; one loud chord, then the sound dies away

notice: At ≈ 6:37, listen for the violins’ wavering figure from the first seconds of the quintet. The circle closes.

threads.title: Beginning and end
threads.body: The violins’ opening figure frames the whole work: the first bars, the end of the first movement and the last pages of the finale.

threads.title: Five equal voices
threads.body: The clarinet rarely stands apart. It shares tunes with the first violin and the viola, and often plays below the strings.

threads.title: Autumn
threads.body: Most of the quintet is soft, in the minor, and ends quietly. Even the major-key moments are tinged with regret.
